rule.title: Modification or Deletion of an AWS RDS Cluster
rule.author: Ivan Saakov

es.summary: CloudTrail registró una llamada ModifyDBCluster o DeleteDBCluster contra Amazon RDS. Puede ser un cambio administrativo legítimo o un intento de tomar control, exponer o destruir una base de datos Aurora/RDS.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos de CloudTrail con eventSource rds.amazonaws.com y eventName ModifyDBCluster o DeleteDBCluster, sin importar el resultado ni la identidad que hizo la llamada.
es.why_it_matters: Un atacante con permisos RDS puede restablecer la contraseña maestra, cambiar security groups o desactivar la protección contra borrado para extraer datos (ATT&CK T1020, exfiltración automatizada), o borrar el clúster para causar pérdida de datos.
triage_steps: Identifique userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.type, sourceIPAddress y userAgent. Confirme si la identidad suele administrar RDS y si la IP o el user agent son habituales.
Revise errorCode: un AccessDenied indica un intento fallido, pero sigue siendo relevante si la identidad no debería llamar a RDS.
En ModifyDBCluster, revise requestParameters: masterUserPassword, vpcSecurityGroupIds, deletionProtection, backupRetentionPeriod, enableIAMDatabaseAuthentication y applyImmediately.
En DeleteDBCluster, verifique skipFinalSnapshot y finalDBSnapshotIdentifier. Borrar sin snapshot final es especialmente grave.
Busque eventos de la misma identidad e IP en +/- 15 minutos: CreateDBClusterSnapshot, ModifyDBClusterSnapshotAttribute, AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress, CreateAccessKey, AssumeRole.
Compare con tickets de cambio y ventanas de mantenimiento del clúster afectado (requestParameters.dBClusterIdentifier).
Revise alertas previas de la misma identidad o IP y los logs de conexión de la base de datos después del cambio.
false_positives: Administradores autorizados aplicando cambios planificados, como rotación de contraseña maestra o ajuste de retención de backups.
Pipelines de IaC (Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK) que modifican o eliminan clústeres en despliegues.
Eliminación de clústeres de prueba o entornos efímeros como parte de mantenimiento programado.
response_steps: Confirme con el responsable del clúster y el dueño de la identidad si el cambio estaba autorizado.
Si no lo estaba, deshabilite o revoque las credenciales involucradas, invalide sesiones activas y restrinja permisos rds:Modify*/Delete*.
Revierta los cambios: restaure contraseña maestra segura, security groups y deletionProtection; restaure desde snapshot o backup si hubo borrado.
Revise snapshots compartidos o copiados hacia otras cuentas y las conexiones a la base de datos para evaluar exfiltración.
Documente el incidente y active deletionProtection y alertas sobre clústeres críticos.
es.severity_rationale: El nivel alto es adecuado porque estas acciones pueden dar acceso directo a datos sensibles o destruirlos, aunque requieren validar el contexto de cambio.

en.summary: CloudTrail recorded a ModifyDBCluster or DeleteDBCluster call against Amazon RDS. It may be a legitimate admin change or an attempt to take over, expose or destroy an Aurora/RDS database.
en.what_it_detects: CloudTrail events with eventSource rds.amazonaws.com and eventName ModifyDBCluster or DeleteDBCluster, regardless of outcome or calling identity.
en.why_it_matters: An attacker with RDS permissions can reset the master password, change security groups or disable deletion protection to pull data out (ATT&CK T1020, automated exfiltration), or delete the cluster causing data loss.
triage_steps: Identify userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.type, sourceIPAddress and userAgent. Confirm the identity normally manages RDS and the IP and user agent are expected.
Check errorCode: AccessDenied means a failed attempt, still relevant if the identity should never call RDS.
For ModifyDBCluster, review requestParameters: masterUserPassword, vpcSecurityGroupIds, deletionProtection, backupRetentionPeriod, enableIAMDatabaseAuthentication and applyImmediately.
For DeleteDBCluster, check skipFinalSnapshot and finalDBSnapshotIdentifier. Deletion without a final snapshot is especially serious.
Pivot on the same identity and IP within +/- 15 minutes: CreateDBClusterSnapshot, ModifyDBClusterSnapshotAttribute, AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress, CreateAccessKey, AssumeRole.
Match against change tickets and maintenance windows for the affected cluster (requestParameters.dBClusterIdentifier).
Review earlier alerts for the same identity or IP and database connection logs after the change.
false_positives: Authorized administrators applying planned changes, such as master password rotation or backup retention tuning.
IaC pipelines (Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK) modifying or tearing down clusters during deployments.
Deletion of test or ephemeral clusters as part of scheduled maintenance.
response_steps: Confirm with the cluster owner and the identity owner whether the change was authorized.
If not, disable or revoke the involved credentials, invalidate active sessions and restrict rds:Modify*/Delete* permissions.
Revert changes: set a secure master password, restore security groups and deletionProtection; restore from snapshot or backup if deleted.
Review snapshots shared or copied to other accounts and database connections to assess exfiltration.
Document the incident and enable deletionProtection and alerting on critical clusters.
en.severity_rationale: High fits because these actions can grant direct access to sensitive data or destroy it, though change context must be validated.

positive.description: Unknown IAM user resets master password and opens security group on an Aurora cluster via ModifyDBCluster
Cluster deleted with skipFinalSnapshot set to true

negative.description: ModifyDBInstance on a standalone RDS instance, not a cluster action listed in the rule
Read-only DescribeDBClusters call by a monitoring role
